meaning:
ἀπ-αλγέω, -ῶ
1. prop., to cease to feel pain for (Thuc., ii, 61).
2. In late Gk.
(a) to despair (Polyb., i, 35, 5);
(b) to become callous, reckless (Polyb., xvi, 12, 7; MM, VGT, see word): Eph.4:19.†
(AS)
glosses: having lost all sense of shame

renderings.bsb: Having lost all sense of shame

elsewhere.note: They, having become callous, gave themselves up to lust, to work all uncleanness with greediness.
